what: Two truly meshed gear rows (default 22 and 18 teeth) turn slowly in opposite directions, and when scrolling is fast they all speed up together and then settle — the large gears in the closing section and process illustration

options.teeth: This number for each tooth (space-separated), default "22 18"
options.angles: Direction in which the next gear sits from the previous one (degrees, space-separated — last value repeats if short), default 0 (horizontal)
options.speed: Clock speed when idle (rad/s), default .25 — web service page. The app page uses .3
options.ratio: Clock scale applied to the first gear (negative reverses direction), default -0.8
options.hole: Center hole radius (relative to pitch diameter), default .1
options.--fx-a·--fx-b: Alternating sawtooth colors (via style), default var(--kf-accent)·var(--kf-ink)

from.where: Ending of all subpages .mesh (two meshing gears) · service.html #train (four process gears, teeth: 20 13 26 15)

note: The original speeds up only with scroll amount and ignores interaction. Off-screen it pauses drawing but the clock keeps running (so the teeth don’t slip out of alignment on re-entry)
